transcript: HEADER: 2026-03-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m | Recording: Zoom | Meeting title: Monarch Payments - POC scoping (workload modeling)
ATTENDEES: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO, Monarch), Liam O'Neal (Head of Infra), Marta Ruiz (Lead ML Engineer), Ethan Park (PM)

SUMMARY: Quick scoping for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for Monarch's fraud scoring and customer support summarization workloads. Focus on accurate traffic modeling (QPS, concurrency), token distributions, and benchmark plan.
TOPICS COVERED: success criteria, workload sizing, sample traces, benchmark matrix, timeline, security requirements (VPC/KMS/SOC2)
[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: hey everyone thanks for joining, real quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: hi all, Priya here, CTO at Monarch. we'll be driving the POC evaluation from our side - Marta's the ML lead on the models and liam on infra.
[00:16] Sofia Alvarez: great, i'm Sofia AE at Redwood, and daniel here is our SE, he'll run the perf bench and look at the traces, do you want to say hi Daniel
[00:23] Daniel Cho: hey all, Daniel SE, i'll be pairing with Marta on the tokenizer and perf configs, and we'll do the 48 hour runs once we have your traces.
[00:30] Ethan Park: thanks, quick ask - we want to validate both our fraud scoring latency and a summarization chat flow that customer support uses; different QPS / token profiles.

[00:40] Marta Ruiz: yes exactly, on fraud scoring we're looking at synchronous scoring for transactions: typical payload is transaction metadata + a 20-50 token context, model returns a 30-80 token score/justification. latency target sub-200ms p95 if possible, throughput up to about 200 qps during peak windows but average closer to 45 qps across region, also bursts to 450 qps for short periods.

[01:05] Liam O'Neal: infra note: we run in GCP in two regions, primary us-central, secondary europe-west. for POC we can give a 7-day traffic trace and we can spin up a test VPC if needed. security is a hard requirement - KMS usage, audit logs, SSO.
[01:25] Sofia Alvarez: good, that's helpful. can we clarify the two workloads and expected concurrency? fraud scoring is CPU/light model? what's the model size and concurrency estimate?

[01:35] Marta Ruiz: fraud scoring uses a distilled open model, roughly 7B parameters quantized to int8 for cost; at peak we expect 200 qps with concurrency approx 40-60 concurrent requests given our client timeouts and batching. Summarization/chat is a larger 13B family for better quality, avg session prompts are 300 input tokens and response ~220 tokens, QPS lower - avg 8 qps but long tails during business hours up to 30 qps, concurrency 6-12.

[02:05] Daniel Cho: ok that maps to two different serving profiles - a high-QPS low-latency path (7B quantized) and a lower-QPS high-token path (13B). for the POC we'll create a benchmark matrix that varies batch size, kv-cache settings, and quantization flags. we'll also test dedicated vs hosted routing to see cost/latency tradeoffs.

[02:25] Priya Kapoor: success criteria from our side: 1) fraud scoring p95 latency < 200ms for 90% of peak traffic, 2) summarization quality within ±5% of our current baseline BLEU/ROUGE-ish evals (we can share eval prompts), and 3) predictable cost estimates per 1M tokens that match the model.
[02:45] Sofia Alvarez: perfect, we'll codify those. quick question on token distribution - do you have percentiles? avg vs p95 input/output token counts?

[02:55] Marta Ruiz: yes avg input tokens for fraud ~32, output ~48; p95 input 120 tokens if we include extra context, p95 output 160. for summarization avg input 300, output 220, p95 input 1024 (rare), p95 output 800. we do have a tokenizer config and can provide samples.
[03:20] Ethan Park: also note some customer sessions include attachments and multi-turn history which increases tokens; we can mark those as 'heavy' requests - about 8% of traffic.

[03:30] Daniel Cho: good to know - we'll make sure to include a heavy-request bucket in the benchmark. for throughput modeling we usually ask for a 7-day trace with timestamps, request type tags, avg token counts and any session ids so we can reconstruct concurrency patterns.
[03:48] Priya Kapoor: we can provide that - liam can export from our ingestion pipelines. liam is this feasible by monday?
[03:54] Liam O'Neal: yep we can export the 7-day trace, sanitize PII and include sampling for attachments. i'll attach a README for the fields. target upload by 2026-03-23.

[04:05] Sofia Alvarez: excellent. on the Redwood side, we'll run three bench profiles: 1) fraud profile (7B quant, bursts up to 500 qps), 2) summ chat (13B quant/FP16, long tokens), 3) mixed workload (80% fraud, 20% chat). Daniel will share configs and expected metrics.

[04:25] Daniel Cho: for metrics we'll report p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, batch size distribution, cost per 1M tokens estimate using our Optimize profiler. note — transcription: sometimes Redwood product names are mis-typed in transcripts like 'Redwood Dedicate' but it's Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private for VPC.

[04:45] Marta Ruiz: on security: we require KMS integration with our cloud KMS for keys, VPC peering or PrivateLink, RBAC and audit logs. SOC2/ISO compliance is mandatory for go/no-go after POC. can you confirm those are supported?
[04:58] Sofia Alvarez: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC. we'll include SOC2 and ISO docs in the pack. i'll send the security/arch diagram and checklist in the next 24 hours.
[05:08] Priya Kapoor: thanks, also curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated capacity is full do you route to hosted? we need graceful degradation, not 502s.

[05:16] Daniel Cho: we recommend smart routing: we can keep a compatible fallback model variant in hosted mode, return slightly higher latency but prevent errors. we'll demo canary/fallback behavior in the POC.
[05:24] Ethan Park: pricing question - difference between Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted token pricing for these profiles?

[05:30] Sofia Alvarez: i'll include an apples-to-apples comparison: upfront reserved monthly for Dedicated (predictable throughput) vs pay-as-you-go hosted API. we'll show cost per 1M tokens for both and break down GPU hours and estimated batch efficiency.
[05:44] Marta Ruiz: when you run the benchmark, can you test quantization profiles? we see big gains for the 7B but 13B suffers sometimes depending on workload length.

[05:54] Daniel Cho: yes, we'll include int8 and fp16 runs, and test if quantization affects output quality (we'll run eval prompts you provide). we'll also surface recommendation: batch size, kv-cache TTL, and tokenization tweaks.
[06:10] Priya Kapoor: timeline — what's realistic for POC start and completion?

[06:15] Sofia Alvarez: target is start next week we get traces and sign an NDA/POC MOU; bench runs 2 weeks (including 48h perf runs and evals), then 2 weeks for integration & fine tuning, then final review in week 5-6. so total ~6 weeks from trace handoff to review.

[06:30] Priya Kapoor: that works, we'll aim to get trace by 2026-03-23 and expect the MOU signed by friday. one more thing — do you provide client libs for retry/backoff and token counting so our SDKs match Redwood counting?
[06:44] Daniel Cho: yes, we have SDKs and a token-counting utility that mirrors our billing tokenization. we'll share examples and a small test harness to replay traces against your environment.
[06:55] Liam O'Neal: on infra we'll likely test both via VPC/private deployment and hosted to compare latency - can you run the bench in our VPC?
[07:05] Sofia Alvarez: we can run Redwood Private in your VPC for POC — Daniel will coordinate with liam to provision access. for speed we'll parallel-host a hosted run for baseline comparison.
[07:15] Ethan Park: should we schedule a technical deep-dive to go over trace schema and tokenizer specifics?
[07:19] Sofia Alvarez: yes let's do a follow-up with Marta and Daniel. propose tightly scoped 60-min session to go through traces and the eval prompts. suggested date: 2026-03-22, same time?
[07:27] Marta Ruiz: 03-22 works for me. we'll prepare the tokenizer config and a canonical set of eval prompts for quality checks.

[07:33] Daniel Cho: great. i'll prepare the benchmark matrix: axes = model size (7B/13B), quantization (int8/fp16), routing (dedicated/hosted), batch sizes (1,4,8,16), and heavy-request bucket. results will include latency, GPU cost, and quality deltas.
[07:50] Priya Kapoor: outstanding. any red flags? so far the p95 sub-200ms for fraud looks ambitious but maybe achievable with int8 7B and aggressive batching and caching.

[07:58] Daniel Cho: agree it's aggressive but plausible with optimized kernel selection, continuous batching, and prefix/KV caching — we'll test with your real traces to validate. p95 targets will be best-effort for the POC.

[08:10] Sofia Alvarez: quick recap and next steps: 1) Monarch provides sanitized 7-day trace + tokenizer config by 2026-03-23 (owner: Marta/Liam), 2) Redwood (Daniel) runs 48h perf bench and shares results 2026-03-26, 3) Sofia sends pricing and security pack by 2026-03-20, 4) follow-up deep-dive 2026-03-22 to align on traces and eval prompts, 5) POC review week of 2026-03-30.
[08:40] Priya Kapoor: agreed. i'll confirm internal stakeholder list and MOU signature timeline (owner: Priya) - target 2026-03-24.
[08:50] Sofia Alvarez: perfect, thanks everyone. any final quick questions?
[08:55] Ethan Park: none from me, thanks all.
[08:57] Marta Ruiz: thanks, looking forward to the bench results, will send traces soon.
[09:02] Sofia Alvarez: end recording, we'll follow up in slack/email. bye!

POST-MEETING NOTES: Daniel to provision baseline configs and a small replay harness; include heavy request bucket in benchmark; Redwood will show dedicated vs hosted cost delta and fallback routing behavior in the bench report.
REFERENCES/ARTIFACTS: Redwood POC MOU (link shared after call), sample benchmark config (will be attached), security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS docs)
